monotone_godrays.client.enabled.desc: If enabled, the sun and moon cast light shafts past terrain and clouds. If disabled, no rays or lens flare are drawn.
monotone_godrays.client.sunIntensity.des: How bright the sun's rays are. Set to 0 for no sun rays.
monotone_godrays.client.moonIntensity.de: How bright the moon's rays are at night. They follow the moon's phase. Set to 0 for no moon rays.
monotone_godrays.client.quality.desc: How many steps each ray takes toward its light. Higher values give smoother rays, but cost more GPU time for each sun or moon on screen.
monotone_godrays.client.density.desc: How far the rays reach from their light, as a share of the way to it.
monotone_godrays.client.decay.desc: How much light each step of a ray keeps. Lower values give shorter, fainter rays.
monotone_godrays.client.cloudBlocking.de: How much clouds block rays. At 1, a thin cloud blocks about a quarter of the light and a thick one about three quarters. Set to 0 for clouds that block nothing. Has no effect with Fabulous graphics, where clouds never block rays.
monotone_godrays.client.lensFlare.desc: How bright the flare over a sun in view is. Set to 0 for no lens flare.
monotone_godrays.client.fullResolution.d: If enabled, rays are drawn at your game's full resolution. If disabled, they are drawn at half resolution and scaled up, which is about four times faster and looks almost the same.
